newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Countrywide NZ signs US$1 bln note facility.
newsitem.headline: Countrywide NZ signs US$1 bln note facility.

text.p: New Zealand's Countrywide Bank said on Monday it had signed a US$1 billion short and medium term note facility in Hong Kong for its operation there.
Countrywide said in a statement it was one of the largest and most complex facilities ever undertaken by an institution in New Zealand's private sector.
The transaction provides a short and medium term note facility for the Hong Kong branch of Countrywide Corporation, a unit of Countrywide.
The facility, guaranteed by the bank, would allow the branch a degree of flexibility within the Asian market.
Countrywide Bank treasurer Paul Hale said that the facility provided access to a wide range of opportunities in Asia, some of which would benefit New Zealand.

"The Asia-Pacific market promises to be the most dynamic area of growth in the new millennium and, with its incorporation into China later this year, Hong Kong will become an even more important gateway," he said.
Countrywide is a unit of Bank of Scotland.
